subject: Marketplace co-sell: VAT & invoicing responsibilities for multi-entity purchases
messages:
From: Emma Jensen <emma.jensen@cloudretailer.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 08:12:00 +0100
Subject: Clarify: who invoices VAT when customer buys via AWS co-sell?

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — CloudRetailer is excited about the co-sell listing. Before we move procurement forward, our finance team needs clarity on how VAT and invoicing will appear for purchases routed through AWS/Azure/GCP co-sell flows. A few concrete asks: 

- If the purchasing customer selects their local entity during checkout but the marketplace invoice is issued by the cloud marketplace (e.g., AWS Marketplace), which entity is ultimately treated as the billing party for VAT purposes?
- Do we need to collect W-8/W-9 from our buyer or from their purchasing entity?
- For EU customers, is reverse-charge evidence needed from the buyer, or does the marketplace provide settlement documents that satisfy VAT reporting?

Procurement also asked for a short list of the documents Redwood will need from us to complete onboarding (VAT certificate, billing entity GUID, PO templates, etc.). I've attached CloudRetailer’s procurement questionnaire and our VAT cert for your review.

Could you provide a short bulleted breakdown we can share with finance? If easier, feel free to loop in your billing/contact who handles marketplace settlements.

Best,
Emma
Emma Jensen
Head of Procurement, CloudRetailer Inc
Attachments: procurement_questionnaire.pdf (application/pdf); vat_certificate_98765.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Emma Jensen <emma.jensen@cloudretailer.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 11:03:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Clarify: who invoices VAT when customer buys via AWS co-sell?

Hi Emma — thanks for the clear list and the attachments. High level bullets below (short version for finance), followed by a few notes and the docs we usually ask for. I'm copying Vanessa (partner billing) and Karthik (marketplace ops) for any platform nuances.

Short bulleted breakdown for finance (shareable):
- Marketplace flow vs direct flow: if purchase is processed on the cloud marketplace, the marketplace typically issues the customer-facing invoice and handles VAT collection on their platform (marketplace invoice). Redwood receives settlement/remittance from the marketplace as the listing partner.
- VAT liability: depends on the contractual model and the marketplace terms. In many AWS/Azure/GCP listings, the marketplace is treated as the seller of record to the end customer; VAT is collected by the marketplace unless the buyer explicitly purchases a supplier-billed offer. For EU reverse-charge, the buyer must provide a valid VAT number; the marketplace invoice will show whether reverse-charge was applied.
- Multi-entity purchases: we need the billing entity GUID (the entity that will appear on the marketplace invoice) and that entity’s VAT number. If CloudRetailer’s purchaser wants an invoice from Redwood rather than the marketplace, we need to confirm marketplace listing type (BYOL/vendor-seller vs marketplace-managed).
- W-8/W-9 (US tax forms): W-9s are required when Redwood is issuing an invoice to a US entity and the customer requests a tax form; W-8 forms are collected from non-US entities selling/receiving payments if withholding is applicable. For marketplace-driven settlements, marketplace platforms often handle 1099 reporting; we still ask to collect tax-entity forms upfront to cover edge cases.

Documents Redwood will typically request from your procurement team:
- Billing entity name + legal entity GUID used in marketplace checkout
- Registered VAT number (EU) or tax ID (non-EU) + certificate where applicable
- Purchase order (if required) and PO routing instructions
- W-9 or W-8BEN/W-8BEN-E for US reporting (only when Redwood is the invoice issuer)
- Any reseller/partner contract or reseller ID used on the marketplace

Notes and platform specifics:
- AWS co-sell: AWS often issues the invoice to the buyer and handles VAT; however if the listing is set as ‘seller-managed’ we may need to supply a Redwood invoice. 
- Azure/GCP: similar split — check whether the offer is transactable as marketplace-managed or as a BYOL/vendor billed offer.
- Evidence: for reverse-charge on EU sales, the VAT number plus a marketplace invoice that clearly states reverse-charge is sufficient in most jurisdictions. We may also ask for proof of business address if the VAT status is borderline.

I attached our internal marketplace VAT matrix (high-level) to help map the responsibilities per cloud provider and an example DocuSign flow for entity attestation. Can you confirm the preferred billing entity for the purchase and return the completed questionnaire? Once we have that, we can confirm whether the invoice will come from the marketplace or Redwood and advise on which tax forms you'll need to sign.

Next steps:
1) Emma / CloudRetailer to return completed procurement_questionnaire.pdf with billing entity GUID and VAT details.
2) Redwood will validate the listing type and confirm invoice issuer and any withholding actions within 48 business hours.
3) If Redwood will be issuing the invoice, we’ll request the appropriate W-9/W-8 and issue a pro forma invoice for PO processing.

Thanks —
Sean Gallagher
Head of Partner Success, Redwood Inference
Attachments: marketplace_vat_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet), example_docusign_link.txt (link)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 14:18:00 +0100
Subject: Internal: CloudRetailer co-sell — tax routing decision and risk flags

Vanessa / Karthik / Laura — quick internal note following Emma’s procurement questions. Summary and suggested approach: 

Summary: CloudRetailer is buying via AWS co-sell. They’ve supplied VAT cert but haven’t yet confirmed billing entity GUID. Their finance team needs clear instruction on whether to expect an AWS invoice or a Redwood invoice for VAT reporting.

Key risk flags: 
- Multi-entity ambiguity: if purchaser uses an EU subsidiary GUID but CloudRetailer expects Redwood invoice for consolidation, mismatch will cause reconciliation headaches and may require credit memos.
- W-9/W-8 timing: if AWS issues the invoice, they may handle 1099/withholding. But if Redwood ends up issuing the invoice (seller-managed), we must collect W-9/W-8 before invoicing.
- PO routing: customer's PO must match the invoice entity to pass AR validation.

Suggested short-term playbook (for this account):
1) Ask customer to confirm billing entity GUID and whether they selected marketplace-seller vs vendor-billed offer (this is the single source of truth).
2) If marketplace invoices: note for finance that Redwood will receive settlement reports; provide CloudRetailer a short mapping doc of marketplace invoice fields vs Redwood ledger fields (I can draft).
3) If Redwood invoices: request W-9/W-8 and issue pro forma to match PO.
4) For EU reverse-charge: require VAT number + marketplace invoice showing reverse-charge; if absent, Redwood reserves right to invoice VAT and request reimbursement.

Vanessa — can you share any recommended language we should include in the pro forma or the PO guidance to avoid late disputes? Also, do we have an internal checklist for settlement evidence that we can attach?

Thanks,
Sean
(on Sunday morning timezone — replying quickly so procurement can proceed)
